text: In this book's treatment, the cosmological redshift is fundamentally an ordinary Doppler shift set by a galaxy's velocity at the single instant the light was emitted.
explanation: False. The cosmological redshift is a metric effect: photons are stretched continuously by the expansion of space over their entire journey, not shifted once by a velocity at emission. It equals 1 + z = a₀/a_em exactly for any expansion history; only in the small-z limit does it reduce to the Doppler form z ≈ v/c.
